## `forge uv`

Backing module: `Tools.uv_packer`.

```text
usage: forge.py [-h] [--out OUT | --dry-run] [--json]
                [--start-size START_SIZE]
                [--allow-rectangular | --no-allow-rectangular]
                [--uv-scale UV_SCALE] [--max-size MAX_SIZE]
                [--fixed-texture-size | --no-fixed-texture-size]
                [--island-padding ISLAND_PADDING]
                [--require-integer-uvs | --no-require-integer-uvs]
                [--layout {faces,charts}] [--packer {maxrects,shelf,grouped}]
                [--no-recipe]
                bbmodel

Remap UVs in code from current .bbmodel geometry; never paint. An asset with
scripts/<asset>/generate_uv.py runs that recipe instead

positional arguments:
  bbmodel               Current model, including manual geometry edits

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --out OUT, -o OUT     Save a remapped copy to a different path instead of
                        in-place
  --dry-run             Preview packing result without writing any files
  --json                Print the packing result as JSON
  --start-size START_SIZE
                        Minimum square atlas size (otherwise reuse saved
                        options)
  --allow-rectangular, --no-allow-rectangular
  --uv-scale UV_SCALE   Global pixels per model unit: positive integer;
                        explicit value > saved value > default 1. Does not
                        edit the model recipe
  --max-size MAX_SIZE   Maximum atlas side length
  --fixed-texture-size, --no-fixed-texture-size
  --island-padding ISLAND_PADDING
                        Reserved pixels around each packed island; default
                        reuses the saved value, else 1 (aligning with
                        texture_export)
  --require-integer-uvs, --no-require-integer-uvs
                        Require integer vertices, or allow fractions with
                        half-pixel-aligned island centers
  --layout {faces,charts}
                        faces: one island per face; charts: neighbouring mesh
                        faces unfolded together on one continuous texel grid
                        (pixel art across edges; implies fractional UVs).
                        Default reuses the saved value, else faces
  --packer {maxrects,shelf,grouped}
                        maxrects: tightest atlas; shelf: rows in document
                        order; grouped: islands of one block (UV rule block,
                        else parent group) kept together. Default reuses the
                        saved value
  --no-recipe           Ignore the asset's generate_uv.py and pack with the
                        saved options and rules
```

## `forge art`

Backing module: `Tools.art`.

```text
usage: forge art [-h] [--request REQUEST] [--check]
                 {guide,prompt,pull} project

Art requests: ask an external producer (person, tool or agent) for images.

Only when the user explicitly asks for external art; painting normally stays in
the recipe. The project's ``art.json`` describes each image and where it is
delivered; it never says how the recipe uses it::

  {
    "schema": 2,
    "source": "../forge2d/projects/hero/assets",
    "requests": {
      "face": {
        "asset": "hero",
        "description": "Angry glowing eyes, small nose and scowl. Soft painted style, no pixel art; transparent background; ...",
        "pixels": [512, 320],
        "guide": {"element": "head", "side": "front", "points": {"eye_L": [-2.4, 26.5]}}
      }
    }
  }

Per request: ``asset`` (receives the image), ``description`` (everything the
producer must know: subject, style such as pixel art or painted or vector,
transparency, tiling, palette, limits), ``pixels`` (exact delivered size),
optional ``file`` (path inside ``source``, default ``<id>.png``) and optional
``guide`` (``element``, ``side``, ``points`` as [u, v] in that side's axes, element
units). Other keys are kept and ignored.

``guide`` renders the element as seen from the side at the requested size and
records the canvas mapping and point pixels. ``prompt`` prints one ready-to-send
message per request. ``pull`` copies delivered images of the right size from
``source`` to ``assets/<asset>/art/<id>.png``, where recipes read them with
``painter.art(id)``.

positional arguments:
  {guide,prompt,pull}  guide: render guide images; prompt: print the message
                       for each request; pull: copy delivered PNGs
  project              Project directory containing art.json (PROJECT --asset
                       ID limits guide)

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --request REQUEST    prompt: only this request id
  --check              pull: only report; exit 1 when something is not ready
```
